record.original_question: Is it consistent that the dominating number d is singular and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7. Is it consistent that d is a singular cardinal and (d over ω) → (d over ω)^(1,1)_2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{d}$ denote the dominating number, i.e., the least cardinality of a family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \omega^{\omega}$ such that for every $g \in \omega^{\omega}$ there exists $f \in \mathcal{F}$ with $g(n) \le f(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

For cardinals $\alpha, \beta$, the strong polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\alpha}{\beta} \to \binom{\alpha}{\beta}^{1,1}_2$$
asserts that for every coloring $c : \alpha \times \beta \to 2$ there exist sets $A \subseteq \alpha$ of order-type/cardinality $\alpha$ and $B \subseteq \beta$ of order-type/cardinality $\beta$ such that $c$ is constant on $A \times B$.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that $\mathfrak{d}$ is a singular cardinal and at the same time
$$\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$$
holds?
artifact.category_tag: polarized partition relations and cardinal invariants
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that polarized partition relations involving the dominating number and singular cardinals are an active area studied by Garti and Shelah. Related consistency results are known (e.g., the strong polarized relation for singular μ that is a limit of measurable cardinals, and results on the dominating number at singular cardinals), but no source directly verifying a resolution of this specific problem (consistency of $\mathfrak{d}$ singular together with $\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$) was found.

status_evidence.title: A strong polarized relation
status_evidence.snippet: The strong polarized relation is consistent with ZFC for a singular μ which is a limit of measurable cardinals.
status_evidence.claim: Related consistency results for strong polarized relations at singular cardinals are known, but do not directly settle the case of μ = d.

status_evidence.title: Dominating numbers at singular cardinals
status_evidence.snippet: The dominating number at singular cardinals has been studied; for a singular cardinal λ, d_λ > λ.
status_evidence.claim: The behavior of the dominating number at singular cardinals is an active topic, but the specific polarized-relation question remains unverified as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Partition Calculus and Cardinal Invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of polarized partition relations and cardinal invariants by Garti and Shelah.
status_evidence.claim: Background on polarized relations and cardinal invariants relevant to the problem.
